sections.h2: What changes when a Mount Prospect house goes on the market?
sections.html:
Mount Prospect is a Cook County village, so a sale here can carry transfer charges at three levels: state, county and village. The village stamp is its own step, apart from county recording, so schedule it early.

The village sits about 20 miles northwest of downtown Chicago and roughly 4 miles north of O'Hare Airport, partly in Elk Grove Township and partly in Wheeling Township. The Metra station and the closeness to O'Hare are the location points most listings lead with.

Owners here usually pick between an agent, an investor who pays cash, or a sale handled alone. The facts below apply to all three.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Mount Prospect homes?
sections.html:
Mount Prospect recorded 56,852 residents in 2020. The Bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 55,395 is 2.6 percent under its base figure. All of that fits within 10.72 square miles of land, or about 5,304 people for each one.

Census estimates for 2020 to 2024 put the midpoint home at $397,400 and midpoint rent at $1,502. Owner costs run $2,619 monthly with a loan and $1,046 without. Households number 21,600, averaging 2.56 people; 68.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the midpoint household brings in $101,720.

Nearly 30 percent of residents (29.6) were born abroad, and 43.1 percent of those age 5 and up use another language at home. A listing written in more than one language may reach more people. Among adults 25 and older, 48.6 percent hold a bachelor's degree or beyond.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Mount Prospect houses?
sections.html:
Several elementary districts divide the village, and the district for your address often matters more to buyers than the village name. Confirm it before you advertise.

  • Central Mount Prospect: Mount Prospect School District 57.
  • North and somewhat east: River Trails School District 26.
  • South and somewhat west: Elk Grove Community Consolidated School District 59.
  • Small northern, north central and northwest pockets: Buffalo Grove-Wheeling CCSD 21, Arlington Heights District 25 and Prospect Heights District 23.

Township High School District 214 covers the whole village. Prospect High School is the only district 214 high school inside Mount Prospect, and some students attend Elk Grove High School or Buffalo Grove High School. Park services also vary by address, with the Mount Prospect, Arlington Heights, Des Plaines, Prospect Heights and River Trails park districts all serving parts of the village.

sections.h2: How do transit, jobs and shopping help a Mount Prospect sale?
sections.html:
Commuters board Metra's Union Pacific Northwest Line in the village: southeast to Ogilvie Transportation Center, northwest toward Harvard and McHenry. Pace buses cover local routes.

Employment is local too. The village's 2025 financial report lists CVS Caremark and Robert Bosch Tool Corporation as its largest employers, followed by the Village, Mount Prospect School District 57, Township High School District 214, Rauland-Borg, Costco, Walmart, School District 59 and TJX. Randhurst Village is the best-known retail address, and companies based in the village include Cummins Allison, NTN USA and Rauland-Borg.

The village counts as entirely urban. Its climate is humid continental, with muggy summers and snowy winters, in plant hardiness zone 5b, which is why inspectors look hard at roofs, sump pumps and furnaces.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes apply when a Mount Prospect house sells?
sections.html:
The Cook County Clerk's transfer fee listing starts with two charges: the State of Illinois at fifty cents for each $500, and Cook County at twenty-five cents for each $500. The seller is named as the liable party on both. The state figure matches 35 ILCS 200/31-15.

The village adds a real estate transfer tax of its own, paid by buying a stamp. Finance, on its Taxes and Service Fees page, offers an online stamp application and in-person stamps by appointment, along with a rebate form and an affidavit of no consideration for exempt transfers such as taking a person off a deed. Call Finance for the current village rate and the party responsible, since both come from the Village Code.

The Clerk's site also has a lookup that shows the transfer fee for each municipality in the county, handy for comparing neighboring towns. Put all three charges in your net sheet early.

sections.h2: How are Mount Prospect property taxes billed?
sections.html:
Cook County splits each year's property tax into two bills. The Treasurer's schedule lists April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026 for tax year 2025, and both have passed. Earlier years landed on other days, so rely on the date printed on your own bill.

The title company typically splits the year's tax between buyer and seller from the latest bill, so bring that bill and your parcel number. The Treasurer's site also describes homeowner, senior, senior freeze, disability and disabled veteran exemptions that a qualifying buyer may look into afterward.

Finance also describes a property tax relief grant for qualifying single-family owners, a rebate on part of the village share of the county bill. Call to learn whether it is open before counting on it.

sections.h2: Which disclosures and village rules apply to a seller?
sections.html:
Illinois puts the disclosure duty in 765 ILCS 77/20: report completed, report delivered, all before a contract is signed. Local buyers also ask about permit history on additions, finished basements and mechanical work.

The Village Code is posted online through the village's code library, and Community Development is the office for permit, inspection and code questions. For a rental, ask the village what license or inspection covers your address before you list.

  • Request permit records for work done during your ownership.
  • Resolve open code notices, since an unresolved notice can complicate the closing.
  • Confirm the water, sewer and refuse account status with the village before closing.

Any past basement water belongs on the report, with repair invoices on hand.

sections.h2: How do the three ways to sell compare in Mount Prospect?
sections.html:
Listing through an agent reaches the most people, with showings, inspections and a lender's schedule attached. Where household income at the median is $101,720, an updated house in a favored school zone may attract competing offers.

  • Agent: fits a house that shows well and an owner able to wait out a standard closing.
  • Owner sale: skips the listing fee but leaves the disclosure form, contract and stamp paperwork to you.
  • Cash purchaser: fewer conditions and a closing date you may help choose, at an offer reduced for needed repairs.

Whichever you pick, get the offer on paper and settle who pays each transfer charge.

faqs.q: Does Mount Prospect have its own transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Finance sells the village's transfer stamps, online or in person by appointment. Ask it for the current rate and the responsible party, because the village sets this apart from the state and county charges.

faqs.q: How much is the Cook County transfer fee?
faqs.a: The Clerk lists twenty-five cents per $500 for Cook County and fifty cents per $500 for the state, with the seller liable for each.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Mount Prospect house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Central areas are in District 57, north and east areas in River Trails District 26, south and west areas in District 59, and small northern pockets in Districts 21, 25 and 23. Township High School District 214 covers the whole village.

faqs.q: What if I need to remove someone from a Mount Prospect deed?
faqs.a: Finance links an affidavit declaring no consideration for exempt transfers like taking a person off a deed. Ask Finance whether your situation qualifies.

faqs.q: When are Cook County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's schedule gave April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026 for tax year 2025. Other years use different dates, so compare against your own bill.
